min_balance.description: The account's floor, in ledger sign: the nightly forecast scan emits `forecast.shortfall` when the 30-day projection drops below it (e.g. `500.00` to be warned before checking goes under $500; a credit card, negative when owed, takes a negative floor such as `-4500.00`). Checking, savings, cash and credit-card accounts only (422 otherwise); at most 4 decimal places.
min_balance.title: Min Balance

AccountOptions.description:
Per-file-account import knobs. ``cutoff``: import only rows strictly older
than this date (null = import everything). ``invert``: flip every amount.
AccountOptions.title: AccountOptions

AccountUpdate.description:
Rename / re-describe / hide / move a real account (DESIGN §3.4).
``hidden`` toggles the display-only ``hidden_at`` timestamp; ``path``
moves the account and everything beneath it (decision 72).

``feed_start`` (§7.1, decision 40) is admin-only: explicit null clears,
absent leaves unchanged (model_fields_set distinguishes the two).
``feed_invert`` (§7.1, decision 43) is admin-only feed configuration
too; a plain bool, so absent/None simply leaves it unchanged.
``drift_basis_override`` (§7.3, decision 83) is admin-only as well, with
``feed_start``'s explicit-null-clears rule. ``holdings_source`` (§8,
decision 88) is admin-only too; absent/None leaves it unchanged.
``min_balance`` (§3.4, #466) is write scope, with the explicit-null-clears
rule.

drift_basis_override.description: Pin the ledger basis the post-sync balance-drift check compares this account's bank balance on: `posted_only` (the bank leaves pending charges out of its balance) or `pending_inclusive`. An explicit null clears the pin and the basis is learned from the account's sync history again; absent leaves it unchanged. Admin scope; checking, savings, cash and credit-card accounts only (422 otherwise).
drift_basis_override.title: Drift Basis Override

holdings_source.description: Where this brokerage account's holdings come from: `feed` (the SimpleFIN snapshots) or `manual` (positions recorded by hand, priced daily, and projected into the same snapshots). Switching to `manual` keeps every feed snapshot as history; the first manual snapshot is dated the day after the last feed one. Switching back to `feed` needs a feed mapping (422 without one) and changes no snapshot: the hand-tracked holdings stay in effect until the first sync after the switch, which ends them from its own date (a position the feed does not report ends there); positions stay, read-only. Admin scope; brokerage accounts only (422 otherwise).
holdings_source.title: Holdings Source

min_balance.description: The account's floor, in ledger sign: the nightly forecast scan emits `forecast.shortfall` when the 30-day projection drops below it (e.g. `500.00` to be warned before checking goes under $500; a credit card, negative when owed, takes a negative floor such as `-4500.00`). Checking, savings, cash and credit-card accounts only (422 otherwise); at most 4 decimal places. An explicit null clears the floor, and the account leaves the shortfall scan; absent leaves it unchanged. Write scope.
min_balance.title: Min Balance

path.description: Move the account to this ltree path, e.g. `liabilities.citicard`. Accounts beneath it move along and keep their relative paths. Refused with 409 when an account already sits at or under the new path, and with 422 for a malformed path or a destination under a category root such as `expenses`. Categories keep their paths.

include_user_categorized.description: Automation correcting automation is fine; overriding a human is opt-in.

The two bank legs keep their exact, unequal amounts (the incoming principal positive and smaller than the outgoing cash) and the difference books to this category. Omit for an ordinary transfer (opposite amounts).

EncryptionStatus.description:
Read-only posture block (issue #123). Field-level Fernet encryption is
mandatory (startup fails closed without a working key), so this mostly
attests rather than warns. Since #137 the narrative layer (payee names,
descriptions, memos, schedule names, audit/event payloads) is encrypted
too; only the numeric skeleton (amounts, dates, statuses, ltree paths, ids)
and the readmodel v2 views over it stay plaintext by design (decision 36).
Storage-level encryption remains a deployment concern the app can't attest.
EncryptionStatus.title: EncryptionStatus

ImportCounts.description:
Per-file-account disposition of rows (DESIGN §7.2). The preview counts for
a request equal the commit's per-account results for the same request.
``in_file`` is the sum of the other buckets, ``uncleared`` excepted;
``skipped_scheduled`` counts Quicken reminder rows (not history, never
imported); ``skipped_investment`` counts QIF ``!Type:Invst`` records
(investment actions, never bank rows; decision 84); ``promoted`` counts
rows that posted an ``expected`` row an earlier import left, because the
file now marks them cleared (per leg for a transfer); ``uncleared`` is the
subset of the created rows that land ``expected`` because the file marks
them uncleared (decision 60). ``split_transfers`` (QIF ``S[Account]``
lines carved out of split rows as transfers) and ``split_remainders``
(split rows whose lines left part of the amount unexplained, booked to
the uncategorized placeholder) are sub-counts too (decision 87).

A recorded reconciliation (issue #268), re-checked against the ledger

leaving the reconciled-through marker silently wrong.

``statement_balance`` is the figure as the statement shows it (positive =
money held; for a credit card, the amount owed). Every other amount is in
ledger sign (a card is negative when owed).

User-facing SimpleFIN sync schedule (UTC).

Presets rather than raw cron. ``hour``/``minute`` apply to ``daily`` only;
the interval presets are anchored so every choice lands a fresh sync just
before the 06:45 UTC matching job, and ``hourly`` (24 runs/day) sits
exactly at the SimpleFIN Bridge budget — the per-connection fetch guard
fails soft beyond it.

TransactionOut.description:
Flat view: the real-account delta plus category path.

With a perspective account (the register view: `GET /transactions?account=X`)
the amount is that account's signed leg; without one, transfers present
their outgoing side with a positive amount (the historical shape).

A row is a transfer only when its postings are a shape Purser creates
(DESIGN §3.3): a plain transfer, or a split loan payment — whose
`category_path` is the interest/fee category and `remainder_amount` that
posting's amount. Any other multi-posting row is not a transfer.

A split transaction (one real leg plus several category legs, such as an
imported Quicken split; decision 87) has `category_path` null and
`split_lines` set to its category-leg count; the legs are in the detail's
`postings`. Split rows are read-only.

convention.description: How `value`'s sign reads. `ledger` (default): as Purser stores it, a loan negative when owed. `statement`: as the statement prints it, a loan POSITIVE when owed (a credit balance is negative); Purser negates it into ledger sign, the same conversion reconciliation applies. A property reads the same either way.
convention.title: Convention

value.description: The account's value on as_of, in ledger sign unless `convention` says otherwise: a property is positive, a loan is NEGATIVE while money is owed. A positive value on a loan is rejected (422) rather than recorded as an asset.
value.title: Value

info.description:
Purser is an AI-native personal finance backend: a double-entry ledger behind a
flat API. Agents are first-class clients — prefer the MCP endpoint at `/mcp`
(same Bearer tokens), or use these REST endpoints directly.

Conventions: amounts are decimal strings (negative = money out); accounts and
categories accept a UUID or an ltree path; posted transactions are immutable
(edits become linked reversal pairs); writes need the `write` scope and are
audited and reversible. Aggregate questions (spending, net worth,
forecasts) have dedicated endpoints — never sum transaction rows client-side.
info.summary: The finance backend for the personal agent stack.
info.title: Purser

patch.description:
Rename / re-describe / hide / move a real account, or set its floor.

``min_balance`` sets (or, with null, clears) the floor the nightly
forecast scan checks; the next scan uses it. A new ``path`` moves the
account and every account beneath it, keeping their relative paths; the
move is audited (`account.move`) and emits `account.moved`. Balances and
history are unaffected: transactions point at accounts by id.

409.description: The new `path` is taken: an account already sits at it or beneath it.

get.description:
Balance at end of ``as_of``. Open loan/property accounts answer with
their latest valuation at or before that date (decision 42); open
brokerage accounts add their latest holdings market value on top of the
postings basis (decision 50); everything else answers from the stored
running balances (decision 37), never recomputed. 0 before first
activity; closed accounts answer for their whole history.

Balance history for one account over ``[start, end]``, one point per
transaction that moved it, plus the ``opening`` balance carried into the
window.

REST is not token-budgeted, so this is the full per-change series — the
downsampled, narrated form is MCP ``balance_history``. Both compose on
the same service functions, so they can never disagree. ``truncated`` is
set rather than silently dropping the tail past 5000 points.

post.description:
Close a real account: void expected instances, post a guided balancing
adjustment (when nonzero), unmap any feed link, then make it read-only.

get.description:
The account's positions, each valued as of today. A feed-sourced
account lists the positions recorded while it was tracked by hand, if
any; they are read-only until it is switched back to manual.

schema.title: Response List Positions Accounts  Account Id  Positions Get

post.description:
Open a position on a brokerage account whose holdings are tracked by
hand (`holdings_source` `manual`; 422 otherwise). 409 while an open
position in that symbol exists, and 409 when the new position would hold
shares on a day a CLOSED position in the symbol held them or sold out
(positions never overlap: start the new one after it). With `quantity`,
it also records the opening `set_quantity` on `as_of`.

Reconcile a checking, savings, cash or credit-card account to a statement
balance (issue #268).

Purser compares the statement figure with its own balance on ``as_of`` in
the chosen ``basis`` and posts ONE adjustment for the difference, dated
``as_of``, to the system category ``expenses.reconciliation_adjustments``.
The adjustment lands in the review set so a person sees it. When the ledger
already matches, nothing is posted and the clean reconcile is still
recorded. Either way ``reconciled_through`` advances and an
``account.reconciled`` event is emitted.

Safe to retry: the same date, balance and basis returns ``created: false``
while the ledger still matches, and 409 ``reconciliation_moved`` with the
difference once a backdated change has moved it. ``GET /accounts/{id}``
and ``GET /accounts/{id}/reconciliations`` re-check recorded
reconciliations the same way on every read.

409.description: The request contradicts a recorded reconciliation. `detail.code` is `reconciliation_moved` (this exact reconciliation is recorded, but the ledger balance on that date has changed since — `detail.difference` = ledger minus target), `reconciliation_conflict` (a different balance or basis is recorded for that date), or `reconciliation_out_of_order` (the date is before the account's latest reconciliation).

get.description:
An account's reconciliations, newest first, each re-checked against the
ledger now: ``in_balance`` is false (and ``difference`` nonzero) when a
later write changed the balance on that date.

schema.title: Response List Reconciliations Accounts  Account Id  Reconciliations Get

post.description: Reopen a closed account so it accepts writes (and corrections) again.

schema.title: Response List Valuations Accounts  Account Id  Valuations Get

post.description:
Record a loan or property account's value on a date: the balance it
reports (its latest valuation replaces the postings sum). Any other
account type is refused (422): its balance comes from its transactions,
plus holdings for a brokerage account. The answer's `value` is in ledger
sign whichever `convention` the request used.

parameters.description: only calls that disclosed fields beyond the privacy defaults
parameters.name: disclosed

schema.description: only calls that disclosed fields beyond the privacy defaults
schema.title: Disclosed

get.description:
Virtual sessions: per actor, split after 30 minutes of silence.
Web session tokens naturally span their lifetime; long-lived API/MCP
tokens split into conversation-shaped bursts; System = scheduler jobs.

Reveal the encryption key ONCE, for the wizard's record-your-key step
(the wizard holds an admin session right after POST /auth/setup). 410 Gone
after acknowledgment bounds the exposure window — afterwards the key lives
only in the operator's environment.

post.description: Record that the operator stored the key; the reveal endpoint goes 410.

schema.title: Response Acknowledge Encryption Key Auth Encryption Key Ack Post

post.description:
Password sign-in; sets the session cookie.

Throttled per email and per client address (DESIGN decision 59): after
repeated failures an attempt gets 429 with a `Retry-After` header (whole
seconds) and the password is not checked. Failed and throttled attempts are
audited as `auth.login_failed` / `auth.login_throttled`.

429.description: Too many failed sign-ins for this email or client address. Refused without checking the password; retry after `Retry-After` seconds.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until a sign-in attempt is admitted again.

get.description:
Public probe: which sign-in methods the login page should offer.
Password auth is always available; SSO reflects the effective OIDC state
(env defaults + runtime Config overrides). Exposes nothing but booleans.

schema.title: Response Auth Methods Auth Methods Get

get.description:
The provider's redirect back. The state must match the cookie set by
`/auth/oidc/login`; the id_token is validated before any account lookup.

Start an SSO sign-in: redirect to the provider with a fresh state,
nonce and PKCE challenge, kept for the callback in a short-lived cookie.

get.description:
Durable event replay — a subscriber that was down for a day catches

Deterministic daily balance projection with annotated events —
'checking goes negative on the 19th' is answerable in this one call.
Instances beyond the materialized horizon are expanded from the rules
(`projected`), so `days` is honoured up to 365; `coverage` says what the
line is made of. Every event names its `basis`; an estimated one carries
a `range` band (min/max of its schedule's newest settled amounts and its
own), and then each day carries `low`/`high` — the balance with every
ranged event at its worst / best — and `pessimistic_low`/`optimistic_low`
their minimums. `first_shortfall` stays on the point series.

Latest snapshot set per brokerage account (cost basis + market value),

post.description:
Create a bill/income schedule, active. With `propose=true` it lands
a SUGGESTION instead (`status='proposed'`, `suggestion_id`) that the
user's decision turns into the schedule. A proposal for a payee or
counterparty the account already has a schedule for is refused (422,
naming that schedule).

Scan import history for recurring payees and land the patterns in the
suggestions inbox (#233); re-running refreshes open rows and never
re-proposes what was rejected. Nothing activates here.
Materialize expected instances for all active schedules (idempotent).

Record a credit card's statement balance against the payment it is due
on. The payment instance takes the statement balance (both legs move, the
card's leg = the balance), is pinned so the current-balance estimate no
longer moves it, and reports `basis: statement`; the statement, its
closing date and who recorded it stay on the instance. Recording again
replaces it; resetting the instance removes it. Credit cards only — a
loan payment is an ordinary override (`PATCH /transactions/{id}`).

patch.description:
Edit the rule. Live un-pinned instances follow (slots the new rule no
longer produces are voided and released, amounts re-estimated, missing
slots materialized); pinned instances keep their amounts and dates. A new
`name` or `payee` relabels every live instance — pinned ones too — whose
description or payee still equals the old one; labels you changed stay.

post.description: Terminal: no more instances, history kept.

Stop expecting: live un-pinned instances are voided and their slots
released; resume brings them back.

The inbox: open suggestions by confidence (snoozed ones hidden until
their date unless include_snoozed). `kind` narrows it to schedules, to

post.description:
accept / edit_then_accept apply the draft: a schedule suggestion
creates the schedule (active, materialized); a transfer_link suggestion
creates the rule as a DRAFT and returns `projected_links` — activate it
through POST /rules/{rule_id}/state with that count confirmed. reject is
durable and scoped; snooze hides it until a date. Nothing ever
auto-accepts, and nothing here activates a rule. A match suggestion's
accept confirms the proposal (marking its bank row reviewed) and reject
rejects it for good; it has nothing to edit. If its proposal is already
gone the suggestion is withdrawn and the call answers 422.

get.description:
List the tokens the caller may manage (DESIGN decision 75).

A session (a signed-in person) or an admin-scoped token sees every token of
its own user; any other token — an agent's — sees only itself. Dead tokens
(expired, revoked, idle-timed-out sessions) are hidden by default;
include_expired reveals the rows retained as audit/attribution anchors
(DESIGN §9).

delete.description:
Revoke a token (audited as `token.revoke`; DESIGN decision 75).

Any token may revoke itself. A session (a signed-in person) may revoke
every token of its own user, and an admin-scoped token any token. An agent
token without admin scope can revoke only itself: any other id gets the
same 404 as an unknown one, so the answer reveals nothing.

patch.description:
pending/expected edit in place; posted becomes an atomic
reversal + replacement pair. category='[account]'
converts the row to a transfer; a plain category on a transfer converts
it back (send `account` = the side that keeps the row). An amount on an
expected/pending transfer is the leg of `account` (a schedule instance
defaults to its schedule's account) and moves both legs, never the
direction; a posted or bank-linked transfer is refused with how to
correct it.

post.description:
Hand a schedule instance back to its rule: unpinned, with the rule's
date (its slot), name, payee and current estimate — both legs of a
transfer. When the rule no longer produces the slot, or estimates
nothing, the instance is voided and its slot released instead. Live
instances of active schedules only.

Undo a transfer merge/absorb: resurrect the voided bank rows (their
content hashes move with them, so re-imports stay no-ops) and suppress
the automatic relink paths.

Void an expected or pending row. A voided schedule instance keeps its
slot filled, so the occurrence is skipped. Voiding a pending that a match
names settles the match: a confirmed match is released and its instance
is expected again in its slot, override kept; a proposal is withdrawn. A
posted row cannot be voided directly — correct it or merge it.

delete.description:
Remove a user's SSO link (admin scope; audited as `user.unlink_oidc`).

A linked account refuses a different subject from the same provider, so
this is how an administrator lets someone sign in with a new identity at
that provider. The account and its password, if any, are kept; the next
SSO sign-in that asserts the account's verified email links it again.
404 for an unknown user, 409 when the user has no SSO link.
